MR. CHAIRMAN: Question No. 123. 
Loss of Revenue due to Ban on Smoking 
*123. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the total loss during the current year to the Government exchequer 
due to ban on smoking at public places an d ban on sponsorships of sporting 
events by tobacco firms;' and 
(b) in what manner Government propose to bridge the gap of revenue 
shortfall? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN): (a) Sir, The revenue Collection (which 
is mainly from central excise duty) in respect of tobacco products has shown 
an upward trend in the first quarter of the current financial year, as compared 
to the corresponding period last year. 
(b) Does not arise, in view of the above. 
(SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Sir, we all know that regulations on 
tobacco advertising and sponsorship of sports etc. are said to have hurt a 
section of business community. The Government put a ban on advertising 
and sponsoring sports events by tobacco firms, but the motive is defeated 
because major companies like ITC, Godfrey Phillips, VST, GTC etc. have 
already started setting-up of

RAJYA SABHA [31 July, 2001] 
surrogate brands to promote their flagship brands. I would like to know as to 
how the minister is going to deal with the situation. I demand that there 
should be a maximum excise duty on tobacco-related products. The Finance 
Bill, 2001 imposed, some additional levi es on cigarettes and tobacco-related 
products. The revenue, so collected, w ill go to the National Calamity Relief 
fund. I would like to know from the hon. Minister whether he would be kind 
enough to part with, at least, 15 per cent of the total revenue, so collected, for 
the welfare of the tobacco growers in the country, particularly in A.P. 
SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN: Sir, already, our Government 
has introduced a Bill to prohibit peop le who smoke at public places, from 
smoking at public places ...(Interruption)... It was referred to the Standing 
Committee, but it has yet not been legislated. We are waiting for the report of 
the committee. Except Delhi, Sikkim and Goa, no State in the country has 
enacted laws to prohibit people from smoking at public places. 
The hon. Member has also asked about the collection of revenue. Till now, 
there is no Central legislation to prohibit people from smoking at public 
places. Hence, it is not possible to quantif y the loss of revenue at this stage. 
Sir, in the financial year 2000-2001, up to June 2000, we had collected a total 
revenue of Rs. 1,133.11 crores from cigarettes. In the financial year 2001-
2002, up to June 2001, we have collected a total revenue of Rs. 1,201.58 
crores from cigarettes. Hence, there is no loss of revenue in respect of 
cigarettes. The Central Government has also imposed additional duties for 
the natural Calamity Relief Fund. 
Sir, we are collecting that amount for the natural Calamity Fund. The Hon. 
Member had asked whether this amount would be utilised for the welfare of 
the employees working in the cigare tte industry. The Government will 
examine his request. 
DR. Y. LAKSHMI PRASAD: He was talking about the tobacco growers. 
He had requested you to help the tobacco growers, not the company 
employees. 
SHRI   GINGEE   N.   RAMACHANDRAN:   Sir,   the   reply   is

DR. KARAN SINGH: Sir, the hon. Minister sounded somewhat apologetic 
about the fact that tobacco production was not going to fall. Cigarette 
smoking is one of the major health hazards in the world today. Lakhs of 
people die every year directly as a result of cigarette smoking. Any 
enlightened, Government would move towards a ban or maximum possible 
reduction of cigarette smoking. Sir, you might remember that when I was the 
Health Minister, we introduced a da nger sign on every packet. Now it is a 
farce. You go to any area in Delhi toda y. You will see huge advertisements 
glamorous boys and girls smoking and a tiny illegible thing written in one 
corner saying, "Cigarette smoking is dangerous". Sir, everybody knows that 
foreign companies are now dumping their cigarettes here in huge numbers. 
They give cigarettes free to the young people so that they become addicted. 
This is a major health hazard. I have all sympathy for the tobacco growers. I 
agree that some alternative proposal should be made for that. But, for the 
health of the nation, will the hon. Mini ster please assure the House that he 
would not look upon this as a financial resource? He may as well be making 
money out of dead bodies. This is a matter in which I feel a certain passion 
and a certain commitment is required.

*121. SHRIMATI SAROJ DUBEY: Will the Minister of CIVIL 
AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of bilateral agreements which Air India entered with various 
airlines during the last two years;

of these bilateral agreements; 
(c) the details of seat adjustments utilized by Air India and other airlines; 
(d) whether it is a fact that the Air In dia lost a large number of seats of 
other airlines as a result thereof; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) 
and (b) Bilateral Air Services Agreemen ts are entered into by Governments 
and not airlines. Prior to 1999, India had finalised bilateral Air Services 
Agreements with 93 countries. Under

capacity entitlement for both countries. Prior to 1999, about 31.8 million

More rights to Malaysian Airlines 
*125. SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA: Will the Minister of CIVIL 
AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Malaysian Airlines has been given more rights than they 
had asked for in bilateral airlines talks concluded some time back; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that Government had ordered an enquiry into this 
matter; and 
(d) if so, the findings thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) 
to (d) No, Sir. During the bilateral air services negotiations held in 
September, 2000 between Government of India and Government of 
Malaysia, Malaysian Government had requested a total increase of 4800 seats 
per week which was not agreed to and it was decided to increase the capacity 
entitlement for each side by 1500 seats only resulting in a total entitlement of 
3900 seats per week for each side. This  was done keeping in view the high 
seat factor of 84% of India-Malaysia route. Due to shortage of aircraft with 
national carriers, it was also agreed that Malaysian Airlines may operate 
additional 1200 seats per week against the unutilised capacity entitlement of 
the Indian side subject to commercial agreements with national carriers. 
Whenever our national carriers wish to operate these seats, Malaysian Airlines 
will have to withdraw accordingly. Till then the national carriers will gain 
financially by such utilisation of 
30 

[31 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
Indian  entitlements by  Malaysian  Airlines.  Last enhancement of capacity 
was done in 1990. 
Operation of Malaysian Airlines to Mumbai was made conditional to their 
operation from the newly declared international airports of Bangalore and 
Hyderabad. In exchange, national carriers will also be able to operate to two 
additional tourist points of Malaysia, namely, Penang and Langkawi. 
Moreover, Indian side has also gain ed a connect code share arrangement 
from Mumbai, Bangalore and Hyderabad all the way to West Coast of USA 
through Kualalumpur with a facility to discharge and pickup passengers at 
Kualalumpur (5th freedom rights). Further, designated Airline of India shall 
be able to exercise 5th freedom tra ffic right from Kualatampur to Jakarta, 
Auckland in New Zealand and two points in Australia. 
In view of the above, the arrangement reached between India and Malaysia 
are quite balanced and satisfactory.

Loss suffered by AAI 
*136. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the observations of 
Comptroller and Auditor General of India regarding the loss suffered by Airports 
Authority of India in finalizing bids for awarding of a contract for running duty 
free shops; and 
(b) if so, what steps have been taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) 
and (b) The Comptroller and Auditor General, in its report has observed that the 
contracts for Duty Free Shops could not be awarded to highest bidder due to 
Management's lapse in inviting bids for running the Duty Free Shops departmental^ 
without having expertise for the same and obtaining financial bids in an erroneous 
manner from the existing parties for the original tender, and AAI had to forego 
a total revenue of Rs. 168.75 crores upto June, 2000. The facts of the matter in 
this regard are as under: 
In June, 1995, AAI had invited pre-qualification global tanders for selection of 
consultant/consolidators to assist the AAI to set up Duty Free Shopping 
Arcades in the additional areas identified at the five international airports of Delhi, 
Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata and Thiruvananthapuram. In January, 1996 a 
Committee felt that AAI did not have sufficient experience in the running of duty 
free shops. Therefore, the committee deci ded to select a concessionaire for 
running duty free shops and shortlisted four parties from the bids r eceived. 
Accordingly in August, 1996, AAI asked those shortlisted 
46 

[31 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
parties to submit financial bids. They were asked to submit bids for setting up duty 
free shops not only in the additional area identified in the begining at the five 
international airports but also in new Terminal-2C at Mumbai, which was under 
construction. In June 1996, broad terms and conditions were finalised. In August 
1996, financial bids were received. M/s Lion City Holding, Singapore bid 
highest for Terminal-2C while M/s Weitnaur Switzerland bid highest for 
additional area. All the bidders were asked to match with the highest offer in 
respect of the two segments. M/s Lion City Holding, who had been ranked 
higher in the technical presentation offered to hike their offer to match with M/s 
Weitnaur and were, therefore, asked to revalidate their Earnest Money 
Deposit (EMD). M/s Lion City did not revalidate their EMD and therefore 
their offer got invalidated. It was also decided to delink Terminal-2C at Mumbai 
as it was still under construction and also to consider the offer M/s Weitnaur. 
While negotiating the contract terms with M/s Weitnaur, AAI noticed some 
legal infirmity in tender procedures i.e. the pre-qualification for tenders 
invited in 1995 were for consultant/ consolidators to assist AAI, whereas the 
final proposed award was for concessionaire. In May, 1998 AAI took a decision 
to reject the tender due to this legal infirmity. If the tenders had been awarded, it 
would have led to legal complication and court cases.

all flood affected regions in various States.

the problem of floods in the country. The Rashtriya Barh Ayog (RBA) set up 
in 1976 examined the problem in detail and submitted its report in 1980. The 
recommendations of R.B.A. which form the framework for flood management 
strategy in the country, were forwarded to all the State Governments for 
implementation.

953. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOWDA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE 
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that due to the present Export Import Policy, India 
will be a place for dumping ground; and

THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI 
MURASOLI MARAN): (a) and (b) The present five year Export and Import 
Policy was announced on 31.03.1997. India's export growth rate during 
1997-98 was 9.5% during 1998-99 was 7.4%, during 1999-2000 was 14.17% 
and was 26.39% in 2000-2001 (in rupee terms). Similarly, the growth rate of 
imports during this period was 11% in 1997-98, 14.2% in 1998-99, 13.6% in

73 

RAJYA SABHA [31 July, 2001]

apprehensions regarding India becoming a dumping ground are not borne 
out by facts. 
However, export promotion is a constant endeavour of the government and 
export growth is being constantly monitored. Export policy and strategy is 
formulated accordingly. In this direction, a number of steps have recently 
been taken. These include reduction in transaction cost through 
decentralization, simplification of proc edures and various other measures as 
enumerated in the Exim Policy. Steps have also been taken to promote 
exports through multilateral and bilateral initiatives. Further, Special 
Economic Zones (SEZ) are being set up to boost the exports. The measures 
announced, in amendments to Exim Policy, on 31.03.2001 include promotion 
of agricultural exports through setting up of Agri Export Zones, improvement 
in market access, setting up business- cum-trade facilitation centre and trade 
portal besides strengthening the present duty remission schemes like advance 
licence scheme, duty free replenishment certificate, duty entitlement 
passbook scheme etc.

AND INDUSTRY (DR. RAMAN): (a) and (b) Following are the schemes being 
implemented by the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion, Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry for the development of industrially backward areas in 
the country; 
(1) Growth Centre Scheme: 
Under this scheme 71 growth centres are proposed to be developed throughout 
the country which would be provided with basic infrastructure facilities like 
power, water, telecommunication, sewage, effluent disposal etc. enabling them to 
attract industries. The growth centres approved by the Government of India are to 
be developed by the State Governments with Central assistance of Rs. 10 crores 
per centre (Rs. 15 crores in the case of North-Eastern region). The scheme 
introduced during 1988 has been extended to the 9th Five Year Plan Period. 
(2) Transport Subsidy Scheme: 
This Scheme was introduced in July, 1971 to promote industries in hilly, remote 
and inaccessible areas. The scheme is applicable to the States of Himachal Pradesh, 
Jammu & Kashmir, the North-Eastern States, Sikkim, Union Territories of Andaman 
& Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep, Darjaling district of West Bengal and 
eight hill districts of Uttaranchal comprising Almora, Chamoli, Dehra dun, 
Nainital, Pauri Garhwal, Pithorgarh, Tehri-Garhwal and Uttar Kashi. Under the 
scheme, subsidy ranging from 50% — 90% is admissible of transport costs incurred 
on movement of raw materials and finished goods from designated rail heads 
/ports up to the location of industrial units and vice-versa for a period of five 
years from the date of commencement of commercial production. The scheme has 
been extended up to 31.3.2007.

Norms for Opening Post Offices 
1. Norms for opening Extra Departmental Branch Post Office: 
Population: In Normal Areas: 
3000 population in a group of villages [including the Proposed Post Office (PPO) 
village] 
In Hilly,  Tribal, Desert and Inaccessible Areas: 
500 population in an individual village or 1000 population in a group of 
villages. 
Distance: In Normal Areas: 
The minimum distance from the nearest existing post office will be 3 Kms. 
In Hilly,  Tribal, Desert and Inaccessible Areas: 
The distance limit will be the same as above except that in Hilly Areas, the 
minimum distance limit can be relaxed by the Directorate in cases where such 
relaxation is warranted by special circumstances which should be clearly 
explained while submitting a proposal. 
Anticipated Income: In Normal Areas: 
The Minimum anticipated revenue will be 33 1/3%  of the cost. 
In Hilly, Tribal, Desert and Inaccessible Areas: 
The minimum anticipated income will be 15% of the cost. 
2. Criteria for upgrading/opening Departmental Sub-Post Offices: 
(a) In Rural Areas: The minimum work-load of the Extra 
Departmental Branch Post Office, proposed to be upgraded, should 
be five hours per day. The permissible limit of annual loss is 
Rs. 2400/- in Normal Rural areas and Rs. 4800'- in Tribal and Hilly 
areas. 
(b) In Urban Areas: In Urban areas, the post office should initially 
be self-supporting, and, at the time of the first annual review, it 
should show a 5% profit to be eligible for further retention. 
The minimum distance between two post offices should be 1.5 Kms 
109 

RAJYA SABHA [31 July, 2001) 
in cities with a population of 20 lakhs and above, and 2 Kms. in other Urban 
Areas. No two delivery offices, however, should be closer than 5 Kms. for 
each other. 
Heads of Circles have powers to relax the distance condition in 10% of the 
cases. 
A Delivery Post Office in Urban Area should have a minimum of 7 
Postmen's beats.

COMMUNICATION (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) There have been no violation of the tender norms and no loss 
has been caused to the Government on account thereof. The Notice inviting 
Tender (NIT) for induction of additional cellular operators in various service 
areas in the country was floated on 9.3.2001. The pre-qualification bids

were evaluated in accordance with the conditions prescribed in the tender 
document. 
The eligibility criteria as contained in Clasue 5.1 (vi) of the Tender 
Document provided that "Any number of Indian Companies as well as foreign 
Companies may join together to promote the joint venture bidder company. 
However, an Indian company or a foreign company cannot be part of more 
than one such joint venture bidder company. The same Indian company in its 
sole capacity can bid either by itself or through its joint venture company." 
While evaluating the pre-qualification bids it was found that two Reliance 
group companies namely, M/s. Reliabl e Internet Services Limited and 
Reliance Communications Private Limited had submitted 
118 

[31 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
their bids for 15 Service Areas each. Fo rm the equity structure of these two 
companies, it was found that none of their partners arc common and as such 
there was no violation to the eligibility criteria prescribed in the Tender 
Document. However, in order to ensure fair competition, all the bidders were 
asked to confirm that there is no common interest of any of the 
partners/promoters/constituents in any other bidding company who has bid 
for the same service area and in case their is any common interest, only on 
bid for a service area shall be consider ed. They were given option to retain 
only such bids so as to ensure fair competition. In response to this, M/s. 
Reliance Communications Private Limited chose to withdraw all the bids 
submitted by them for 15 Circles. This was allowed to the company. The 
Earnest Money Bank Guarantee (EMBG) and Financial Bids were returned 
to the company before the first stage Financial Bids were scheduled to the 
opened. Withdrawal of the bids by M/s Reliance Communications settled the 
matter. Allowing both the bids would have given rise to unfair competition 
leading to subsequent stages of financial bidding as infructuous. EMBG can 
not be forfeited in the situation where a bidder is disqualified in the pre-
qualification stage or opted to withdraw the bids in terms of option given by 
the Government. 
(d) Docs not arise in view of (b) and (c) above.

second report relating to capital restructuring and reforms was submitted in 
July, 2001. 
152 

[31 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
The main features of the scheme recommended by the Expert Group for 
one time settlement of outstanding dues are a$ under:— 
(a) 50 per cent waiver of surcharge/interest on delayed payments; 
(b) For the remaining dues i.e. the entire principle outstanding as well as 
the remaining 50% surcharge, bonds could be issued by the respective State 
Governments; 
(c) The bonds could be issued through RBI at a tax free interest rate of 
8.5%; 
(d) The bonds should be structured to achieve a moratorium of 5 years on 
repayment of principle with the entire principle being repaid between the 6th 
and 15th year; 
(e) the bonds shall be identical to bonds issued in connection with the 
market borrowings of State Governments, with the attendant discipline in 
repayments. The bonds will be subject to lock-in-restrictions that will allow 
release of only 10 per cent of the bonds in the secondary market each year; 
(f) For ensuring timely payment of current dues in future, defaults in 
current payment for power/fuel should  attract a graded reduction in the 
supply of power from central power stations and in coal supplies. Where 
such defaults exceed 90 days from the date of billing the Ministry of Finance 
should recover these dues through adjustment against releases due to them 
from the Centre; 
(g) As part of the scheme, SEBs should accept, reform-based 
performance milestones such a setting up of SERCs, metering of 
distribution feeders and improvement in revenue realization. The 
milestones should be specified in the MOUs to be signed with the 
Ministry of Power; 
(h) The states should be offered incentives for complying with the scheme. 
If SEBs do not default on their current dues and adhere to the performance 
milestones, CPSUs should pay them, during the first four years commencing 
from 1.4.2001, bi-annual incentives equal to 2 per cent of the value of bonds; 
(i) Further, if SEBs open and ma intain LCs till the end of December, 
2001, CPSUs should pay them a one time cash incentive 
153 

RAJYA SABHA [31 July, 2001] 
equal to 2 per cent of the value of bonds; 
(j) In addition, States undertaking reforms should also be assisted through APDP 
grants and discretionary allocation of Power; 
(k) This scheme should enter into force only after one-half of the States that 
have an annual billing of over Rs. 500 crore per annum from CPSUs give their 
consent, and should be effective in respect of the States that give such consent; 
and 
(1) The States that withhold their consent beyond 60 days after this scheme 
enters into force should be  denied any share in the discretionary allocation of 
15 per cent from the Power stations of CPSUs as well as any assistance under 
APDP. If the overdues of such States exceeded to Rs. 50 crores in respect of any 
CPSU, they should also attract reduction in power and coal supplies, as applicable to 
the States participating in this scheme. 
Following the submission of the Report of the Expert Group a high level 
Empowered Group consisting of Finance Minister, Dy. Chairman, Planning 
Commission, Minister of Power and Chief Ministers of some States met on 
26.6.2001 and 6.7.2001. The Empowered Group endorsed the 
recommendations of the Expert Group with the following modifications:— 
(i) Waiver of surcharge would now be 60% instead of 50% as recommended 
by the Group; and 
(ii) The incentives for achieving the reform based milestones should be 
increased to 6% in the first year and 5% in the second year. 
Recently, Minister of Power has written to Chief Minister of States and 
UTs urging them to initiate necessary steps for implementation of the scheme 
at the earliest.

set of brokers and sub-brokers acting on behalf of a common set of clients who

Executive Director was also debarred from holding public office in any capital 
market related public institution for a period of three years. In the third phase, 
investigations were completed against Harshad Mehta, BPL, Videocon and 
Sterlite by October, 1999. Show cause notices were issued to them in 
December, 1999. The parties were given opportunity of final hearings in the 
month of March/April 2001. Pursuant to the hearings, SEBI passed orders on

proceedings through some of their directors/officials were ordered under section

Dandewala gas field. Out of the two we lls drilled, one was dry and the other

areas, as also explore in the deeper layers of the producing fields.

new technologies for seismic surveys, work over, stimulation 
operations, drilling of wells etc. in producing areas. 
In any field, generally a combination of various efforts are implemented 
simultaneously and' thus it is difficult to attribute oil gain to any individual

Protection of Jorhat District of Assam from Brahmaputra River 
1081. SHRI DRUPAD BORGOHAIN:  Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) what action has been taken by Government to protect the North-Eastern 
Part of Jorhat District from the Brahmaputra; 
(b) how much fund had been released for the purpose and how was it utilised; 
(c) what is the new proposal about funding; and 
(d) whether Government would undertaken the work directly? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRIMATI BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY): (a) To protect North 
Eastern part of Jorhat district from flood and erosion 
203 

RAJYA SABHA [31 July, 2001] 
of river Brahmaputra, the State Govt, of Assam has undertaken 7 nos. flood 
management schemes on south bank of river Brahmaputra and for protection 
of Majuli island a total estimated cost of Rs. 44.66 crore. 
The Brahmaputra Board under this Ministry has prepared Master Plan of Majuli 
island in which different long term measures for protection of Majuli island from 
flood and erosion of Brahmaputra have been identified. Based on the Master 
Plan, a detailed project report for protection of Majuli island from erosion of 
river Brahmaputra has been prepared by  Brahmaputra Board at an estimated 
cost of Rs. 243.64 crore. 
(b) Flood Management being a State subject, flood control projects are planned, 
funded and executed by the State Governments themselves out of their own 
resources and as per their own priorities. The assistance as being rendered by the 
Central Government are technical, catalytical and promotional in nature. The 
Central Government has been extending Central Loan, Assistance to the State 
Govt, of Assam since 1972—74 onwards. An amount of Rs. 390.94 crore as 
loan and Rs. 10.09 crore as Grant-in-aid have been released to the State Govt, 
of Assam upto March, 2000. An amount of Rs. 1.31 crore has been released by 
the State Govt, of Assam during 2000-2001 by undertaking the about mentioned 
six nos. short term flood management schemes in the North-Eastern part of Jorhat 
district. 
(c) A Centrally Sponsored for funding the flood control schemes in 
Brahmaputra and Barak basis with 90% Central share as grant and 10% State share 
is presently under the consideration of the Full Planning Commission. The 
Planning Commission also releases the funds to the North-Eastern States for 
various schemes under Non-lapsable Central Pool of Resources. 
(d) No, Sir.

Workshop on International Water Management 
1083. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: WUI the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) what is the outcome of the three day International workshop in 
International Water Management recently held in Bangalore; 
(b) whether Government propose to fonnulate National Water 
Policy; and 
206 

[31 July, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) if so, by when the policy is likely to be formulated and announced? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRIMATI BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY): (a) A three day 
International Workshop on Integrated Water Management was held on 21—23 
June, 2001 at Bangalore. The important outcomes of the workshop are: to 
provide opportunities for an open dialogue among water planners and managers and 
communities in attempting to manage water resources; to share successful water 
resources management experiences a nd technologies for dissemination of 
information; capacity building for Integrated Water Resources Management 
(IWRM); to define strategies for the future to be taken by governments, 
academics and NGOs towards sustainable and integrated water resources 
management planning and action; and sustainable action projects implementing 
principles of IWRM. 
(b) and (c) The National Water Policy has been adopted in September, 
1987 by the National Water Resources Council (NWRC) headed by the Prime 
Minister with Chief Ministers of all the States, Chief Ministers/Administrators of 
Union Territories and Union Ministers of water related Ministries as members.

TRIBUTES TO SHAHEED UDHAM SINGH 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, today is the anniversary of the 
martyrdom of Shaheed Udham Singh, who was hanged this day, 61 years ago, 
for killing Sir Michael O'Dwyer, who was Governor of Punjab when the 
Jalianwala Bagh firing took place on Ba isakhi day in 1919. Shri Udham 
Singh sacrificed his life for the Honour of his country and his contribution to 
inspiring the youth of the country and for attainment of India's freedom will 
always be remembered. It is because of  the sacrifices of  martyrs like Udham 
Singh that India is, today, an independent nation. Let us pay our respectful 
homage to his sacred memory. 
I request Members to rise in thei r places and observe silence in the 
memory of Shaheed Udham Singh.

SHRI YASHWANT SINHA: As I go along in my reply. I shall try 
to deal with various points which have been raised by the hon. Members in 
this House. But I would like to begin by putting forth certain facts in proper 
perspective with regard to the UTI and with regard to the US-64 Scheme. The 
first and the most important issue -- because this is something which has been 
raised in this House and outside -- is the issue of what happened to the money 
of the US-64 Scheme. A general impression has been created as if this money 
had vanished somewhere and that some people have pocketed this money and 
that it was not available. Let me ha sten to add that what actually has 
happened was that the value of the stocks held under US-64 Scheme has 
declined. So. the overall value of the fund has declined. It still has a corpus. It 
still has a value. As we go along, I am quite sure, it will achieve the levels 
which it had before the 30th June this year. 
We have, that is, the UTI has, come out with a redemption scheme 
which will be operational from tomorrow. And we have said that the 
Government stands fully behind the UTI. as far as the redemption or even a 
better redemption in future is concerned. So, nothing has happened to the 
corpus. It is not that somebody has walked away with it. It is only that its 
value has declined because its value is su bject to the fluctuations of the stock 
market. Now, why is it subject to the fluctuations of the stock market, Sir? It 
is subject to the fluctuations of the st ock market because, over a period of 
time, this fund, the US-64, became largely an equity fund. What is the nature 
of this US-64? It is not an assured-income scheme. But it is a regular income 
scheme. There are three features which distinguish this scheme. 
The first is, people who invest in the units 'Gt US-64 make capital 
gains. They purchase at a price and sell at a price which is higher. Secondly, 
they receive annual dividend from the UT I. And thirdly, it provides liquidity. 
It is almost like cash because, if you are holding units, you can go to the UTI 
offices, tender your units and get money for it. So, liquidity is a very, very 
important feature of this particular scheme. When the UTI announced the 
freeze on the 2 nd of July, it is this part wh ich suffered a major set back, 
namely, the liquidity of the scheme was supposed to be restricted for a period 
of six months, which the investors did not like, and a situation arose which 
we are now trying to correct.
